reasoning: The garbled strings occur before the actual printed title page in the raw OCR stream.

Internet Archive reports that this item was machine-OCRed with Tesseract; the document is detected as French, but the recorded OCR parameter is -l eng, an English-language model mismatch that can further degrade recognition.
The archive metadata also marks an early bookplate leaf; non-body-text front matter, stamps, decorative marks, skew, bleed-through or typography can generate pseudo-words of exactly this kind.
The meaningful bibliographic text begins later with SERVICE DES ANTIQUITES DE L'EGYPTE / ANNALES / TOME III / LE CAIRE / 1902.
No semantic reading of the strings as Egyptian, a cipher, a ritual formula or transliteration is admitted without image-level verification against the underlying scanned leaf.
normalized_interpretation.working_reading: Machine OCR noise from front matter; preserve it as provenance evidence, but do not promote it into a semantic signal.

first_verified_body_text.article: Fouilles autour de la pyramide d'Ounas (1900-1901). IX. Sur les bijoux d'époque saïte trouvés à Sakkarah
first_verified_body_text.author: Gaston Maspero
research_relevance: The article documents rich Saite-period funerary jewelry from Saqqara.
It explicitly describes gold sheaths/covers for the twenty fingers and toes on the mummy of Zannehibou.
This is useful as a control for Egyptian funerary metal body-part coverings and for workshop/material context.
It does not by itself document a genital sheath, the Osiris phallus, CG 53469, or a Mendes provenance chain.

next_checks: Acquire or inspect the exact early scanned leaf corresponding to the garbage OCR and map marks-to-tokens visually.
Inspect Plates I-III of the Maspero article and the preceding Barsanti discovery report cited there.
Search this volume for additional gold body-part covers, containers, sealed/hollow objects and Osirian/Sokarian funerary contexts.
Keep all findings separate from the CG 53469/Mendes claim unless an explicit catalogue or provenance bridge is found.

verdict: The strange text visible in both screenshots is almost certainly machine-OCR garbage from early front matter, not an ancient encoded text. The valuable signal is the volume itself: it contains an early primary archaeological report on Saqqara funerary gold and body-part covers that is relevant as a control corpus.
